# Overview

This report analyzes gamma-band (25–58 Hz) activity on intracranial macro-bipolar (macBP) channels in the **Dupi** intervention cohort, locked to breaths and sniffs, and asks which gamma measures are **stable across controls** while **separating controls from Dupi**, **separating responders from non-responders**, or **tracking olfactory recovery** across sessions.

**Cohorts.** Dupi = intervention, up to three sessions per participant (S1/S2/S3). **Control = OBEControl (OBE)**. The EEGbreathing (EEG) cohort is **excluded** — those recordings carry no nasal/depth electrode on which to measure gamma.

**Design decisions baked in (before external review):**

- Best macBP channel selected per recording by **peak power after FOOOF spectral flattening in 25–58 Hz** (highest gamma).
- Superlet time-frequency power (fractional adaptive, base cycles 3, order 3–30), validated to machine precision against the reference `faslt`.
- Ridge tracked with the **Frequency_ridge_tracking** forward–backward algorithm (ported to MATLAB), on the per-breath within-frequency z-scored power (`myChanZscore`, no baseline).
- **Both** whole-window z (as specified) **and** a pre-inhale baseline z are computed, so burst/peak results can be checked against Cohen's normalization-window concern.
- **Per-breath FOOOF** (aperiodic exponent/offset + periodic gamma peak presence) so a "gamma" claim is not confused with a broadband 1/f shift (Voytek).
- Per-breath **breathing/airflow covariates** (inhale volume, duration, peak flow) and `goodBreath` QC are carried, to address the sniff-airflow confound (Zelano).
- Group statistics **aggregate to session level first** (each session = one observation), avoiding trial-count bias (Cohen).

# Behavioral olfactory performance

Scores follow the lab's validated formulas: cue **d′** (signal = cue==odor; log-linear corrected), threshold **air-calibrated PEA intensity**, O15 **identification accuracy** (`sum(expScore)/15`). breathingTask has no olfactory score. Points are colored by responder status (defined below); black bars = session means ± SE.

```{r beh-plots, fig.show="hold", out.width="49%"}
for(p in c("beh_cue_d.png","beh_thresh_lowcal.png","beh_o15_acc.png","beh_composite_all3.png"))
  if(hasfig(p)) knitr::include_graphics(file.path(Fg,p))
```

---

# Composite Olfaction Index & responder split

The **Olfaction Index** is the mean of three normalized sub-scores (`O15_acc`, `thresh_low_cal/400`, `cue_d/3.5`) for sessions with all three olfactory tasks. Dupi participants are split into **responders** vs **non-responders** by whether the composite **improves from session 1 to session 2**.

```{r resp-table}
kt(rd("responder_table.csv"), "Responder / non-responder classification (composite S2 vs S1)")
```

```{r comp-plot, out.width="60%"}
if(hasfig("beh_composite.png")) knitr::include_graphics(file.path(Fg,"beh_composite.png"))
```

# macBP gamma channel selection

For each recording, the **peak flattened power in 25–58 Hz (dB over the FOOOF aperiodic fit)** is shown for every macBP channel; the **maximum per recording is bold** (the selected channel). We also report whether the selected channel had a **FOOOF-detectable gamma peak**, and how many non-selected channels did.

```{r macbp-table}
mw <- rd("macbp_table_wide.csv")
if(!is.null(mw)){
  chanCols <- grep("^macBP", names(mw), value=TRUE)
  disp <- mw |> select(sessID, task, cohort, all_of(chanCols), bestLabel, bestGammaDetected, nNonMaxDetected, nMacBP)
  # bold the max per row across chanCols
  m <- as.matrix(disp[,chanCols]); storage.mode(m) <- "double"
  disp <- disp |> mutate(across(all_of(chanCols), as.character))
  for(i in seq_len(nrow(m))){
    r <- m[i,]; j <- which.max(r)
    for(k in seq_along(r)) disp[i,chanCols[k]] <- if(!is.na(r[k]) && length(j)==1 && k==j)
      cell_spec(sprintf("%.2f",r[k]), bold=TRUE) else if(is.na(r[k])) "" else sprintf("%.2f",r[k])
  }
  kbl(disp, escape=FALSE, caption="Peak flattened power (dB) in 25–58 Hz per macBP channel; bold = selected (max).") |>
    kable_styling(bootstrap_options=c("striped","condensed"), font_size=10) |>
    scroll_box(height="520px")
}
```

```{r macbp-summary}
b <- rd("macbp_best.csv")
if(!is.null(b)){
  cat(sprintf("Selected channel had a FOOOF-detectable gamma peak in **%d of %d recordings (%.0f%%)**.\n\n",
              sum(b$bestGammaDetected), nrow(b), 100*mean(b$bestGammaDetected)))
  cat(sprintf("Among non-selected channels, a detectable gamma peak appeared in a mean of **%.2f** channels per recording (of %.1f non-selected).\n",
              mean(b$nNonMaxDetected), mean(b$nMacBP-1)))
  s <- b |> group_by(task) |> summarise(n=n(), selDetected=sum(bestGammaDetected),
        pctSelDetected=round(100*mean(bestGammaDetected),1), meanNonMaxDet=round(mean(nNonMaxDetected),2))
  kt(s, "FOOOF gamma-peak detectability by task")
}
```

# Which measures are good? (low control variability + separation / tracking)

The headline question: measures with **low between-control variability** that also (1) separate control↔Dupi, (2) separate responder↔non-responder, and/or (3) track recovery across sessions. The table below ranks measures by `goodness = |max separation effect| / (1 + |control CV|)`.

> **Important caveat (added after external review).** This first-pass ranking is **not** the final verdict. Three independent reviews showed it is driven by artifacts: the responder↔non-responder separation rests on **n=2 non-responders**; ridge-frequency's low CV is a **bounded-tracker artifact**; the FOOOF-selected channel has a real gamma peak in only **39%** of recordings; and no multiple-comparison control was applied. The **Reviewer-response analyses** section below re-tests everything with bootstrap CIs, peak-gating, airflow regression, and 1/f control — where **0 of 460** control↔Dupi separations survive as CI-significant. Read that section for the corrected conclusions.

```{r goodness}
G <- rd("gamma_top_measures.csv")
if(!is.null(G)){
  disp <- G |> transmute(task, metric,
    control_CV=round(control_CV,3), sep_control_dupi=round(sep_control_dupi,2),
    sep_resp_nonresp=round(sep_resp_nonresp,2), recovery_rho_resp=round(recovery_rho_resp,2),
    goodness=round(goodness,2)) |> arrange(desc(goodness)) |> head(30)
  kt(disp, "Top gamma measures (low control CV × high separation/tracking)")
}
```

```{r top-plots, results="asis"}
tf <- list.files(file.path(Fg,"gamma"), pattern="^top_.*\\.png$", full.names=TRUE)
for(g in head(tf,10)){ cat(sprintf('\n\n![](%s)\n\n', g)) }
```

kt(cg |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~round(.x,3))), "Coupling measures: control CV and separation effect sizes")
```

```

# Robustness & confounds

- **Aperiodic vs periodic (Voytek).** Per-breath FOOOF exponent/offset are tracked; the goodness table includes `apExp` and `gammaBumpDb`/`gammaPeakPresent`, so any group "gamma power" difference can be checked against a 1/f shift.
- **Normalization window (Cohen).** Burst/peak metrics are computed under both whole-window z and a pre-inhale baseline z (`*_base` columns) — agreement indicates the z=3 results are not an artifact of the normalization window.
- **Airflow/sniff confound (Zelano).** Per-breath inhale volume/duration/peak flow are carried as covariates; `goodBreath` QC is applied. (Airflow-adjusted comparisons in the reviewer-response section.)
- **Respiration–gamma coupling.** Session-level Tort MI, preferred respiratory phase (circular), resultant length, and inhale/exhale ratio are computed (`out/gamma/coupling`).

---

# Reviewer-response analyses

These analyses were added to answer the three reviews directly. **Headline result: with session-level bootstrap CIs, no gamma measure cleanly separates controls from Dupi.**

## Honest control↔Dupi ranking (outcome-blind, bootstrap CIs)

Ranked by |Cohen's d| for control-vs-Dupi (the outcome-blind, non-circular axis); `cd_sig=1` only if the 95% CI excludes zero. The largest point-effects are **absolute power** measures (Dupi lower), not ridge-frequency.

```{r hl-cd}
kt(rd("gamma_headline_controlDupi.csv") |> head(15), "Top control↔Dupi separations by |d| (all 0 are CI-significant → underpowered/artifact)")
```

## Is the effect aperiodic? (Voytek)

Dupi show a **steeper aperiodic exponent** than controls (positive d), and absolute-power separations **partially survive** residualizing on the exponent — so the gap is not purely 1/f.

```{r ap-sep, fig.show="hold", out.width="49%"}
kt(rd("gamma_aperiodic_separation.csv") |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric),~round(.x,2))), "Aperiodic exponent/offset: control↔Dupi effect size (d)")
kt(rd("gamma_1f_controlled_separation.csv") |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric),~round(.x,2))), "Power separations: raw vs after 1/f (exponent) control")
if(hasfig("gamma/ap_apExp.png")) knitr::include_graphics(file.path(Fg,"gamma","ap_apExp.png"))
```

## z-window robustness (Cohen) and the "chirp" (Voytek/Cohen)

peakZ depends on the normalization window (low whole-window vs baseline-z correlation), though burst *presence* is robust. The simulation shows a broadband transient + ridge tracker reproduces a wandering mid-band ridge with **no oscillation present**; superlet FWHM ≈ 64–80 ms / 4 Hz.

```{r zconc}
kt(rd("gamma_zwindow_concordance.csv") |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric),~round(.x,3))), "Whole-window vs pre-inhale-baseline z concordance")
kt(rd("superlet_FWHM.csv"), "Superlet effective resolution (impulse-response FWHM)")
```

```{r sim, out.width="95%"}
if(hasfig("gamma/sim_broadband_transient.png")) knitr::include_graphics(file.path(Fg,"gamma","sim_broadband_transient.png"))
```

# Methods & reproducibility

**Adding a participant** is a data-tracking-sheet edit (a row + parameters); the pipeline is sheet-driven end to end. To refresh the analysis: (1) `build_session_index.m` (inventory), (2) `run_scores.m` (behavioral + macBP selection), (3) `run_gamma_all.m` (per-breath gamma; lab, parfor), (4) `assemble_spectrograms.m`, (5) the R scripts `inventory_report.R`, `behavioral_composite.R`, `macbp_table.R`, `gamma_aggregate.R`, then knit `report.Rmd`. All project code lives in `plotsForBruce_2/code`; external tools (`fooof_basic`, `myChanZscore`, Superlets `faslt`, Frequency_ridge_tracking) are called in place.

```{r sessioninfo}
cat("Superlet: fractional adaptive multiplicative, F=22:1:62 Hz, c1=3, order [3 30]; ridge band 25–58 Hz, penalty 1.0.\n")
```
